## Course Overview

Generative AI (Gen AI) and foundational large language models (LLM)
offer extraordinary opportunities to improve our analytical workflow and
daily life. By their design, LLMs are probabilistic: they predict the
most probable combination of characters, words, and sentences that could
follow a **prompt** like a human had written the prompt and what follows
it. Probabilistic nature implies that a single prompt could yield an
infinite number of completions. Therefore, user's objective is to make
AI's responses as deterministic as possible. Precision and accuracy of
the AI's answers determines its usefulness. Therefore, to harness full
power of the AI-Agents, we need to acquire new skills of:

-   Writing effective prompts;
-   Curating model context, and
-   Using right **interfaces/software** for different tasks with AI.

The **objective of this course** is to enable economists who perform
micro-data analysis with Stata/R (Python) to **revolutionize their
workflow** by leveraging context-aware AI assistance and agents. To
achieve this objective, this course will consist of short presentations
and, mostly, practical demonstrations, exercises, and self-study
materials, where we will:

-   Introduce WB-approved software and solutions:
    -   Integrated Development Environment (IDE): Positron
    -   Github.com/Worldbank: Collaboration platform and WB Open Source
        initiative for analysis development
    -   Github Copilot: WB-approved way of using AI assistance
        (GPT/Claude) for coding.
-   Help troubleshoot their installation and use.
-   Discuss key principles and shortcomings of AI assistance in daily
    coding work.
    -   Overview about the technology, its strength and limitations.
    -   Responsible use of AI: securing sensitive data and limiting the
        context.
    -   Effective prompting.
-   Practice key skills of the context-aware use of AI:
    -   In-line code completion: instant boost to your work
    -   AI Assistance: almost a replacement to google with the
        context-aware answer
    -   AI Agents: delegate complex tasks to AI to perform independently
        on your behalf.
    -   Planning coding with AI.
    -   Advanced topics: Custom AI-Agents, Instructions and Skills.
-   Practice AI use on typical use-cases:
    -   Code refactoring, cleaning and commenting.
    -   Reproducibility package preparation.
    -   Reproducing old code using new data.

The course is structured in two 3-hours sessions of (preferably)
in-person and/or hybrid work at the beginning and the end of the week,
and a period of self-study between two sessions with the structured
exercises.

-   **1st session** covers key concepts, troubleshoot software setup
    and usage, and provide a kick-off demonstration on AI capabilities
    for coding and ways of using it. By the end of this first session
    participants should be capable of using AI on their computers
    independently and be enabled to learn it further.

-   **Self-Study period** is meant to provide space and time for
    participants to practice AI use in analysis and get comfortable with
    the software interface and coding workflow. Using clearly defined
    case-studies and examples, course participants are expected to
    resolve problems independently and accumulate questions for second
    session, where these problems will be addressed.

-   **2nd session** is dedicated to practicing specific skills and
    use-cases as well as addressing questions. We will demonstrate use
    of AI for planning and executing complex tasks; practice this with
    the participants, answer their questions, and conclude with the
    demonstration of the more advanced: cutting-edge use cases such as
    agentic code development, testing, and debugging.

To consider the course completed, participants are expected to demonstrate
the ability to use AI assistance for coding independently, and submit
two short case studies on the use of AI assistance for coding during the
self-study period, and in a week after the second session. Their successful
submission is a requirement, which will be used as deliverables for
assessing the course completion.

## Detailed plan

### Prerequisites

- Basic familiarity with Stata/R (Python) and micro-data analysis.

- Installation of Positron IDE and GitHub Copilot (instructions will be
  provided before the course).

  - Engaging with the ITS helpdesk for any software installation issues.

- Setting up a GitHub account, joining the WorldBank organization and
  requesting the access to the GitHub Copilot for WorldBank (instructions
  will be provided before the course).

  - Engaging with [github@worldbank.org](mailto:github@worldbank.org)
    for any issues related to GitHub account setup, access to GitHub Copilot.

### Session 1: Introduction to AI-Assisted Coding

- Live demonstration of a code refactoring task with and without
  AI assistance to show the difference in workflow and output quality.

- Walkthrough of the software interface and usage workflow: troubleshooting
  common issues.

- Overview presentation:

  - AI-assistance technology;
  - strengths and limitations: when DO and DO NOT use/expect AI to be helpful,
  - responsible use of AI;
  - basics of prompting: how to write effective prompts;
  - curating context for AI: how to limit the context;
  - secure sensitive data.
  - Set expectations right: Stata support vs other languages - R and Python.

- Case studies:

  - Refactoring code with AI assistance.
  - Writing with AI: preparing a reproducibility package and documenting code.

- Q&A and discussion.


### Self-Study Period: Practice and Exploration

- During a 2-3 day self-study period, participants will be encouraged
  to perform structured exercises to practice AI-assisted coding,
  document their experiences, challenges, and questions during this period
  to bring to the second session.

- Live Teams channel will be available for participants to ask questions and
  share insights during the self-study period.

- Participants will be asked to submit a case study completed with
  the help of the AI assistance during the self-study period, which will be
  used as one of the deliverables for assessing the course completion.

  Selected case studies for self-study:

  - Reproducing old code using new data with AI assistance.

  - Reproducing analysis following an example with AI assistance.

  - Trying a different language: R or Python instead of Stata with AI assistance.

### Session 2: Every day AI-Assisted Coding and Use Cases

- Addressing questions and challenges from the self-study period.

- Demonstration of planning and executing complex tasks with AI assistance.

- Overview presentation

  - prompt engineering for complex tasks
  - prompt patterns as reusable templates.
  - when to stop using AI and think: recognizing when AI is leading you in circles
  - cost of AI use and token awareness
  - Enhancing the workflow with GitHub and Git-versioning: how to start using
    with the help from AI.

- Practical case studies:

  - Planning and executing complex tasks with AI assistance.
  - Advanced use cases: agentic code development, testing, and debugging.
  - Positron DataBot: agent for fast exploratory data analysis.

- Q&A and discussion.
